The manipulation of the argument ID results in sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit is now public and may be used.

LessPass self-hosted sync server backend before commit 9469b0c lacks rate limiting on the JWT login endpoints /tokens/auth/ and /auth/jwt/create/, allowing unlimited authentication attempts. Unauthenticated remote attackers can brute force passwords or perform credential stuffing against known account emails to obtain tokens granting read and write access to stored profiles.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. Prior to 4.4.3, the afpd Spotlight RPC string unmarshalling path in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c uses sl_unpack_cpx to calculate slen from qlen and the attacker-controlled used_in_last_block value without preventing a negative result. An authenticated AFP client can send a complex string or UTF-16 string element that makes slen negative, and the implicit conversion to size_t causes dalloc_strndup or convert_string_allocate to read beyond the heap buffer. The out-of-bounds read can expose heap data through the RPC response or crash the worker process. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. Prior to 4.4.3, the afpd Spotlight RPC unmarshalling loop in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c subtracts an attacker-controlled subcount from the unsigned count variable in sl_unpack_loop without verifying that subcount is not larger. An authenticated AFP client can place an excessive element count in the sl_unpack_ints, sl_unpack_uuid, sl_unpack_floats, or sl_unpack_date handler, or in a null element, so the subtraction wraps near UINT_MAX and the loop continues reading heap memory at increasing offsets up to toc_offset, which is capped at 65000. The out-of-bounds values can be stored in dalloc structures and returned in the Spotlight RPC response, disclosing heap contents. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.69.1, core/hooks/block-credential-reads.sh, core/hooks/block-egress.sh, core/hooks/block-fs-boundary.sh, and core/hooks/block-mcp-writes.sh pin PATH to /usr/bin:/bin, hard-code jq as /usr/bin/jq, and return success when jq is unavailable there. On systems where jq exists only in a Homebrew path, including affected pre-Sequoia or Homebrew-only macOS installations, the hooks can skip credential-read, network-egress, filesystem-boundary, and MCP-write controls. Native deny rules independently protect some credential paths but do not backstop the egress or MCP controls. An attacker who can influence a prompt, repository, or evaluation flow can use the skipped checks to expose secrets or perform unauthorized tool actions. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Brainstorm Force OttoKit suretriggers allows Server Side Request Forgery.This issue affects OttoKit: from n/a through 1.1.42.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, an unauthenticated attacker can submit the __serverInfoUpdate=1 field while controlling X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto. NukeViet\Core\Server::standardizeHost() did not validate the forwarded host against my_domains, and a trailing slash could preserve an attacker-selected port that server_info_update() used to construct a cURL request in includes/ini.php before authentication. The blind, HEAD-only request uses a fixed path, but it permits internal host and port discovery and can poison cached server_headers. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. In 4.6.00, an unauthenticated attacker can place the configured domain in X-Forwarded-Host while choosing a different destination in the ordinary Host header. The earlier fix validates only the forwarded value in includes/mainfile.php, while set_ini_file() in includes/ini.php constructs an outbound cURL request from the separately retained NV_SERVER_NAME before the ordinary host is rejected. Redirect following can carry the blind request to an attacker-selected private host, port, and path and invoke internal HTTP endpoints. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.01, a super-administrator satisfying the NV_IS_SPADMIN gate can use modules/users/admin/fields.php to store an arbitrary existing PHP function in the func_callback setting for a custom profile field because the callback name is checked only with function_exists() and no allowlist restricts which function may be selected. modules/users/fields.check.php later invokes that function through call_user_func() when the field is validated through registration, profile editing, or administrator editing. Selecting a command-execution function crosses the super-administrator to operating-system boundary and executes commands as the web-server account, while ordinary users can trigger the stored callback after it is configured. Because the remediation validates callbacks only when they are written, upgrading does not remove a malicious callback already stored in the database, which must be cleaned manually. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

MaxKB is an open-source AI assistant for enterprise. Prior to 2.10.7-lts, custom Tool Init Param definitions accept attacker-controlled props_info.rules[].validator strings through POST /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool and PUT /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool/{tool_id}, store them without restriction, and pass them to eval() when the parameter form renders. An authenticated user with the default USER workspace role can store JavaScript and trigger execution by opening the tool's Debug screen before entering or submitting a parameter value. The same Init Param form is exposed to accounts with edit permission on the tool, but execution by a different account was not independently verified. The confirmed script runs in the MaxKB origin; access to another user's bearer token and authenticated account authority is plausible only if that user renders the malicious form. This issue is fixed in version 2.10.7-lts.

G DATA Total Security Backup Service Uncontrolled Search Path Element Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of G DATA Total Security. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the Backup Service. The service restores archives from an unsecured location. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-28666.

A flaw has been found in hankcs HanLP up to 2.1.6. Impacted is the function uncompress of the file hanlp/utils/io_util.py of the component TAR Archive Extraction Handler. This manipulation causes path traversal. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.1.7 is recommended to address this issue. Patch name: feb0f82d12762cf4e687b9926efd90c672857780. You should upgrade the affected component.

The Flutterwave Payments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'form_id' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The storing endpoint is accessible without authentication because the required nonce is publicly exposed on any front-end page rendering the plugin's [flw-pay-form], [flw-pay-button], or [flw-donation-form] shortcodes, allowing any unauthenticated visitor to scrape and reuse it.

The MetForm – Contact Form, Survey, Quiz, Conditional Forms, Form Templates & Custom Form Builder for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'mf-te (the form-builder-chosen name of the Text Editor field)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires a published form containing a Text Editor block; the form's public markup exposes the submission nonce as data-form-nonce, allowing any unauthenticated visitor to satisfy the only submission barrier and store the malicious payload.

The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'textarea-N (rich-text draft value, saved as Save-and-Continue draft meta)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the targeted form to have a Rich-Text Textarea field with Save-and-Continue enabled and public submission permissions — once a crafted draft is saved, the payload executes whenever any user, including an administrator, resumes the draft or opens the Draft ID link from the Forminator Submissions screen.

The Admin Columns plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'url' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has added the Author URL column to the Comments screen layout and that the site accepts unauthenticated comments, both of which are default WordPress and plugin configurations.

The Admin Columns plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The kses sanitization pass in classes/Sanitize/Kses.php uses wp_kses_allowed_html('post') augmented with iframe[src] and the data: protocol; because wp_kses_attr_check accepts any data-* attribute on any allowed tag without inspecting its value, a payload embedded inside a data-ac-tip attribute survives intact and is subsequently assigned to innerHTML by assets/js/table.js, bypassing the apparent mitigation entirely.

The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'upload-1 (the File Upload field's element_id)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is an incomplete fix for CVE-2024-1794; exploitation requires that the Forminator form's File Upload field is left at plugin defaults (no 'custom-files' restriction configured) and that the server maps no Content-Type to the .rtx extension — the default behavior of the Debian/Ubuntu Apache package used by the official WordPress Docker image and many shared hosts.

The EZ SQL Reports Shortcode Widget and DB Backup plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'User-Agent header (stored to comment_agent)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.26.45 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that an administrator has saved a report whose SQL query selects attacker-controlled data such as comment_agent, and that the attacker can identify the saved report's slug — a condition trivially met when the administrator publishes the report on a public page via the [SQLREPORT] shortcode.

The Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the site administrator to have configured the Thickbox lightbox effect with the "Try to apply to all images" context (thumbEffectContext=all_images), and exploitation additionally depends on an administrator approving the attacker's initial comment so that subsequent comments from that author are auto-approved.

The Contact Form to Any API plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'your-message (any CF7 form field)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The malicious payload is stored via a single unauthenticated POST to Contact Form 7's public REST feedback endpoint, which uses permission_callback __return_true and requires no authentication or prior interaction to submit.

The WPBot – AI ChatBot for WordPress & Growth Suite: SEO, AI Writer, Email Marketing, Social Media plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'text' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit is triggered when an administrator opens the Chat Sessions screen, at which point the plugin's bundled Bootstrap 3.3.7 affix data-API passes the attacker-controlled data-target attribute value to jQuery as HTML, executing the injected script in the administrator's session.

The BlockStrap Page Builder – Bootstrap Blocks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 0.1.65 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that the attacker has previously had at least one comment approved for a given name and email address, allowing subsequent comments from that author to bypass moderation under WordPress's default policy; exploitation is also limited to sites using a block theme, which is the WordPress default.

The SchemaEngine AI – AI Schema Markup, Reviews & Rich Snippets for SEO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via WebPage JSON-LD Description in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the target page renders a core/latest-comments block with the displayExcerpt option enabled, causing comment content to be incorporated into the WebPage JSON-LD description output in wp_head.

The SiteOrigin CSS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'class' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires a Contributor-level or higher attacker to store a crafted class attribute value in a post, which then fires when a user with the edit_theme_options capability opens the Visual Inspector on the affected post and clicks anywhere in the preview iframe. Exploitation by unauthenticated attackers requires that a third-party plugin providing wp_kses_post()-filtered unauthenticated front-end submission is installed and configured, and a moderator approves the submission. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

The Unbounce Landing Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.1.6. This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on the proxy error message that is persisted to the 'ub-proxy-error-message' option: unauthenticated attacker-controlled REQUEST_URI data is concatenated into the error string in UBHTTP::stream_request_curl()/stream_request_wp_remote() and stored via update_option(), then later echoed inside a <textarea> on the Unbounce Pages Diagnostics admin page without any escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user (an administrator viewing the Diagnostics screen) accesses an injected page.

The VikBooking Hotel Booking Engine & PMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'inquiry (array keys)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The endpoint's only access gate is a CSRF token that is publicly emitted on the unauthenticated inquiry page, making the injection reachable by any unauthenticated visitor without any precondition beyond loading that public page.

The VikBooking Hotel Booking Engine & PMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'vbf<field_id>' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The WP Fastest Cache – WordPress Cache Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary directory deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the singleDeleteCache function in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Successful exploitation requires either the Custom Permalinks plugin or the GeoDirectory plugin to be co-installed, as these provide the necessary mechanism to write a traversal-bearing permalink value into the database that WP Fastest Cache then consumes without validation.

The WCFM Membership – WooCommerce Memberships for Multivendor Marketplace plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'wcfm_membership_registration_form[store_name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.12.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce required to reach the registration endpoint is publicly emitted on the /vendor-register/ page, making the endpoint fully reachable by unauthenticated attackers without any prior authentication or privilege escalation.

The Thim Kit for Elementor – Pre-built Templates & Widgets for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the Post Comment widget is used with the Text Reveal entrance animation (Elementor class 'ekit--fx-word-reveal') on a Single Post template, and the comment widget must be within the initial viewport; once the first comment by an attacker is approved, or if comment moderation is disabled, subsequent payloads fire automatically for every visitor who loads the affected page.

The Germanized for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing_address.first_name (Store API checkout) → stored on parent order; withdrawal get_first_name() fallback' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.1.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload is planted via an unauthenticated guest checkout order's billing first name through the WooCommerce Store API, with execution triggered by a subsequent unauthenticated withdrawal request submission whose nonce is publicly available on the /withdraw-from-contract/ page.

The WPC Frequently Bought Together for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'variation' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.0.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce protecting the woobt_add_all_to_cart AJAX handler is emitted to all unauthenticated visitors via wp_localize_script, effectively nullifying the nonce as an authentication barrier and making the handler reachable without any login.

The ElasticPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'orderby' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected payload is stored in the ep_query_log transient for up to 24 hours after a single unauthenticated frontend GET request, and only fires when an administrator subsequently opens the Status Report page and expands the Failed Queries panel.

The AutomatorWP – No-Code Workflow Automation, Integration & Webhooks Plugin, now with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'your-message (any CF7 form field used in a form_field: tag)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.0.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to have configured a public 'Guest submits a form' automation whose Send-an-email action embeds a form_field tag, after which the payload fires the next time any user opens the affected automation's email log entry.

The Paid Membership Plugin, Ecommerce, User Registration Form, Login Form, User Profile & Restrict Content – ProfilePress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'reg_bio' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.18.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The reg_bio parameter is accepted by the registration handler's allowlist even when the rendered registration form does not include a biography field, meaning an unauthenticated attacker can supply the payload via a raw POST request without needing a visible biography input on the form.

The wpForo Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[display_name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires public user registration to be enabled (users_can_register=1) and a valid _wpfnonce fetched from the public sign-up page, but is otherwise fully unauthenticated.

The Orphans plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.4.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a two-step comment chain: a benign first comment must be approved under a given name and email so that WordPress's comment_previously_approved mechanism auto-publishes the attacker's payload comment without moderation.

The Swift Performance Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '<attacker-chosen parameter name>' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.7.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires that an administrator has configured at least one Cacheable AJAX Action via the plugin's AJAX Cache feature, a condition attackers can confirm by probing for a swift-performance: HIT response header.

The Accept Stripe Payments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'href of any <a> element containing 'asp_action=show_pp&product_id='' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that a user clicks the attacker-placed comment link to trigger the sink; however, if the non-default 'Prefetch Payment Popup Scripts' option is enabled, execution occurs on page load with no user interaction required.

A vulnerability was detected in eigent-ai eigent up to 1.0.2. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file backend/app/controller/chat_controller.py of the component Local Agent Control API. Performing a manipulation results in missing authentication. The attack may be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 1.0.3 addresses this issue. The patch is named 59f43afcb1b0ba7b2de8c65d585124f196c4aa17. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

@fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, when Fastify routing is configured to be case-insensitive, the router folds the request path to lower case in a way that maps certain non-ASCII Unicode characters to ASCII letters, but @fastify/express matches Express mount paths against the decoded path without applying the same folding. The two disagree, so a request that spells a letter of a mount path with an equivalent Unicode character is routed to the protected handler while the path-scoped middleware mounted on that path never matches and is skipped. An unauthenticated client can therefore reach a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, though only when the application enables case-insensitive routing and the mount path contains an affected letter. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

Admidio from 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains a path traversal vulnerability in DocumentsService::renameFile() that allows authenticated users to move files outside adm_my_files by supplying an unvalidated adm_new_name value. Attackers with folder upload permission can submit ../ sequences to file_rename_save to write files and create directories in arbitrary writable locations, including the web root.

Hysteria from 2.0.0 before 2.9.2 contains an ACL bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated clients to reach blocked UDP destinations by reusing an established UDP session. Attackers can open a session to an allowed destination, then send later packets to localhost or private-network addresses to access internal-only UDP services.

A vulnerability was detected in Surya2Developer Online Shopping System 1.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file product.php of the component GET Parameter Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument p results in sql injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A flaw has been found in jprocms up to 1.7.7. Affected is the function StrUtil.format of the component Database Backup Module. Executing a manipulation of the argument host/port/username/password/dbName can lead to os command injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A flaw has been found in Microweber up to 2.0.20. This impacts the function UserManager::make_logged of the file src/MicroweberPackages/App/Http/Controllers/ApiController.php of the component Generic API Dispatcher. This manipulation causes improper access controls. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.0.21 will fix this issue. Patch name: e639d26e61b989b100f8b6f6bb78c0cecca79b99. You should upgrade the affected component.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Aguila Technologies WP Customer Area customer-area allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects WP Customer Area: from n/a through 8.4.5.
Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in myCred myCred mycred allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects myCred: from n/a through 4.0.3.

Gogs before 0.14.4 on Windows contains a path equivalence vulnerability in isRepositoryGitPath that allows authenticated users with write access to bypass .git directory protection using NTFS aliases. Attackers can create, rename or upload files via aliases like git~1 or .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION to overwrite .git/config or hooks and execute commands as the Gogs process.

msgpackr before 2.1.4 contains an inefficient algorithmic complexity vulnerability that allows remote attackers to cause denial of service by repeatedly re-decoding buffered incomplete values. Attackers can stream a large container of small elements in small chunks to UnpackrStream or decodeIter, triggering quadratic decoding cost that blocks the Node.js event loop.

Faye websocket-driver 0.5.0 before 0.8.0, permessage-deflate before 0.2.0, and websocket-extensions before 0.2.0 contain a decompression bomb vulnerability because messages are fully inflated before maxLength is enforced. Unauthenticated remote clients negotiating permessage-deflate can send highly compressible messages, forcing processIncomingMessage() to allocate excessive memory and crash the server process.

Gunicorn 25.2.0 before 27.0.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the pure-Python ASGI HTTP/1 parser that buffers protocol lines without size limits. Unauthenticated remote attackers can send request lines, headers, chunk-size lines or trailers lacking CRLF to grow worker memory and consume CPU, causing denial of service.

erxes before 3.4.14 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the insurance_api plugin that allows unauthenticated attackers to create, overwrite or delete contract templates via GraphQL mutations. Attackers can inject HTML into templates rendered by headless Chromium during generateContractPDF to pull internal network content into PDFs and exfiltrate customer fields.

Casdoor before 4.27.1 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in decodeSamlMessage that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory by sending unbounded DEFLATE-compressed SAML messages. Attackers can send a small, highly compressed SAMLRequest or SAMLResponse to the /api/saml/logout/:owner/:application endpoint, which inflates to gigabytes and crashes or stalls the server.

Weblate before 2026.11 contains an account takeover vulnerability in the reset_password view that allows unauthenticated attackers to reset victim passwords by abusing case-insensitive Unicode e-mail matching. Attackers controlling a lookalike mailbox using a dotless i or other case-folding variant receive the victim's reset link, since it is sent to the typed address, and set a new password.

Bio-Formats versions before 8.5.0 contain an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability in the Leica Microsystems metadata parsing component (e.g., XLEF). The parser uses an insecurely configured DocumentBuilderFactory when processing Leica XML-based metadata files, allowing external entity expansion and external DTD loading. A crafted metadata file can trigger outbound network requests (SSRF), access local system resources where readable, or cause a denial of service during XML parsing.

A flaw was found in xdgmime. A heap-based buffer overflow can be triggered in _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() in the xdgmimemagic.c file on little-endian systems when an attacker-controlled MIME magic file in a user-writable XDG data location (e.g., in the $XDG_DATA_HOME/mime/magic path) is parsed by an application performing MIME type detection (e.g., via g_content_type_guess()). When performing byte-swap, incorrect pointer arithmetic on the write side causes an out-of-bounds write of 2 bytes, resulting in an application crash or memory corruption.

A vulnerability was found in RPM's rpmbuild tarball processing. When processing a crafted source archive, the getTarSpec() function in tools/rpmbuild.cc passes an attacker-controlled tar archive member name to rpmExpand() as part of a %{basename:...} macro expression. A specially crafted .spec member name can therefore inject RPM macros, including Lua expressions, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running rpmbuild. This can be exploited when a victim or automated build system processes an attacker-controlled source tarball using rpmbuild tarball mode (such as -ts, -ta, or -tb).

A flaw was found in rpm. A local attacker could supply a specially crafted `.gem` filename containing RPM macro syntax. When a user or automated workflow invokes `rpmuncompress -x` on this file, the macro expansion occurs during command construction. This allows the attacker to execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the invoking account, leading to a compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

A stack out-of-bounds write vulnerability was found in gfs2-utils. In gfs2_edit, the di_height field from on-disk inode metadata is used as an array index without bounds checking, causing a stack buffer overflow that may lead to arbitrary code execution when processing crafted GFS2 filesystem images.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: guest_memfd: take the invalidate lock when unbinding a dying file

kvm_gmem_unbind() takes mapping->invalidate_lock only if the
get_file_active() succeeds. When the guest_memfd file is dying, its
reference count is already zero so get_file_active fails and the binding
is removed without holding the invalidate lock.

kvm_gmem_invalidate_{start,end}() checks f->bindings independently to
decide whether to begin or end KVM MMU invalidation. So, the bindings
must therefore remain stable between the two calls. Otherwise, unbind
can remove a binding after start increments mmu_invalidate_in_progress,
but before end finds the binding and decrements it.
Example, unbind race with memory failure:

  CPU 0: memory failure               CPU 1: memslot delete
  ----------------------------------  ---------------------------
                                      (guest_memfd file is dying)
  kvm_gmem_error_folio()
    kvm_gmem_invalidate_start()
      finds binding
      mmu_invalidate_in_progress++
                                      kvm_gmem_unbind()
                                        get_file_active() fails
                                        removes binding
    kvm_gmem_invalidate_end()
      no binding found
      counter stays elevated

mmu_invalidate_retry() then returns 1 forever, so guest page faults
retry without ever installing a mapping and the guest hangs.

Remove the distinction between live and dying files in the unbind path.
Always use slot->gmem.file and take the invalidate lock when it's non-NULL.
Normal unbind callers hold slots_lock, which prevents release from clearing
the pointer or freeing the file state until unbind completes. Final VM
teardown can only see a NULL pointer because guest_memfd pins the KVM until
release has cleared all bindings.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86/mmu: Bug the VM if KVM attempts to walk more levels than the MMU has

Extend the "EFER.LMA && !CR4.PAE" check, which exists largely to guard
against KVM configuring a paging32 MMU with more than 2 levels of paging,
with a very explicit check for exactly that: that KVM isn't trying to walk
more levels of paging than the MMU template provides.  I.e. harden KVM
against all bugs that would cause KVM to generates accesses beyond the
bounds of guest_walker's arrays, regardless of how KVM ended up with the
misconfigured MMU.

Note, don't use w->cpu_role.base.level directly as the paging64 template
only provides two levels of page tables for PAE paging on 32-bit hosts, and
handles the third level by manually emulating the PDPTR access.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rtnetlink: wait for RCU readers in rtnl_link_unregister()

rtnl_link_ops_get() finds ops on link_ops under rcu_read_lock() and only
then takes ops->srcu. rtnl_link_unregister() unlinks ops, then calls
synchronize_srcu() and cleanup_srcu_struct() without first waiting for
RCU readers. A reader that found ops before list_del_rcu() and has not yet
taken ops->srcu is not waited for.

Such a reader then locks a cleaned-up srcu_struct and keeps using ops
after the module that owns it is gone. rtnl_newlink() and
rtnl_dump_ifinfo() both look up ops without RTNL, the latter for any
user that dumps links filtered by kind.

With delays added between the lookup and srcu_read_lock() in
rtnl_link_ops_get(), and before rtnl_link_ops_put() in
rtnl_dump_ifinfo(), running "ip link show type dummy" alongside
"rmmod dummy" on a KASAN kernel gives:

  BUG: KASAN: vmalloc-out-of-bounds in __srcu_read_unlock+0x57/0x70
  Read of size 8 at addr ffffffffc02ff318 by task ip/147
  Call Trace:
   __srcu_read_unlock+0x57/0x70
   rtnl_dump_ifinfo.cold+0x30/0x3b
   rtnl_dumpit+0x7a/0x1b0
   netlink_dump+0x486/0x11b0
   __netlink_dump_start+0x661/0x910
   rtnetlink_rcv_msg+0x611/0x9e0
   netlink_rcv_skb+0x126/0x380
   netlink_unicast+0x605/0x830
   netlink_sendmsg+0x6d0/0xbb0
   __sys_sendto+0x335/0x3a0

Call synchronize_rcu() before synchronize_srcu(), as
rtnl_af_unregister() already does. This should be enough because
rtnl_link_ops_get() is the only RCU walker of link_ops, and it takes
ops->srcu before rcu_read_unlock(), so every reader that found ops is
covered by synchronize_srcu() once the RCU grace period ends. The extra
grace period only costs time at module unload.

Readers and the writer were serialized by RTNL until link_ops got its
own mutex, which is why the missing RCU wait did not matter before.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: fix chunk number of the first chunk in a local quota file

Mounting a crafted OCFS2 image can corrupt kernel memory.  When the
local quota file header of such an image claims zero chunks, the first
quota entry allocated during the mount gets a chunk number taken from a
kernel pointer, and releasing that entry clears a bit far outside the
chunk bitmap.

The write will corrupt the data stored at that address, and the
corruption may lead to a system crash or damage unrelated data. 
Mounting requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN, so it takes an untrusted image, such
as removable media or a loop mount of a file from elsewhere.

Since the chunk number comes from a kernel pointer, the address of the
bit that gets cleared differs from boot to boot, and the issue has been
reported under several titles:

- BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KASAN: use-after-free Write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds Write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KASAN: slab-use-after-free Write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KFENCE: use-after-free write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot

Note that none of these is a use-after-free in the quota code: the
chunk and its buffer head are alive.  The bit that gets cleared lies
far outside the bitmap.  KASAN and KFENCE name each report based on the
object occupying that address, which explains why the same issue is
reported under so many different titles.  In the report I sent, the
address fell in a free page, which KASAN labels use-after-free.

There are known reproducers.  Both a syzkaller and a C reproducer are
available from the Google Drive link [1] in my report thread.  The
issue was found by our modified syzkaller, not a theoretical thing
found by an LLM.  I have not seen it outside fuzzing, so it is not
affecting me in the real world.

The local quota file in OCFS2 is divided into chunks, and each chunk
begins with a header block holding a bitmap of the quota entries that
chunk has handed out.  Chunks are numbered from zero, and that number is
used to convert the file offset of an entry back into a bit position in
the bitmap.  ocfs2_local_quota_add_chunk() appends a new chunk to the
in-memory list and numbers it one past the chunk that was last:

	list_add_tail(&chunk->qc_chunk, &oinfo->dqi_chunk);
	chunk->qc_num = list_entry(chunk->qc_chunk.prev,
				   struct ocfs2_quota_chunk,
				   qc_chunk)->qc_num + 1;

The predecessor is looked up after the new chunk is added to the list, so
if the list was empty, the prev pointer is the list head itself.  The head
is the dqi_chunk member of struct ocfs2_mem_dqinfo and is not a chunk, so
reading qc_num through it lands 16 bytes past the start of the head, on
the dqi_gqinode pointer that follows it.  The first chunk of the file is
then numbered with the lower half of a kernel pointer instead of 0.

The list is empty when the local quota file header claims the file has no
chunks.  ocfs2_local_read_info() takes dqi_chunks from that header without
validating it, so an image with dqi_chunks == 0 takes this path when the
first quota entry is allocated.

ocfs2_create_local_dquot() turns the bad number into a file offset with
ol_dqblk_off(), which shifts a 32-bit block number left by the block size
bits, so the top bits of such a large block number are lost. 
ocfs2_local_release_dquot() turns the offset back into a bit index with
ol_dqblk_chunk_off(), using the full chunk number, so the lost bits push
that index far outside the bitmap, and clearing it corrupts unrelated
memory.

Compute the chunk number before putting the chunk on the list, and use 0
when the list is empty.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: imx-jpeg: cancel timeout worker when streaming stops

Each per-fd context ctx owns a delayed_work (ctx->task_timer, callback
mxc_jpeg_device_run_timeout) armed via schedule_delayed_work() at the end
of mxc_jpeg_device_run() to recover a stalled encode/decode job. The only
existing cancellation is cancel_delayed_work() in the frame-done IRQ
handler, which de-queues a pending work item but does not wait for a
callback that has already started, and it only runs when a frame completes.

When the fd is closed while a job is in flight (the frame-done IRQ has not
fired yet), nothing syncs the worker before mxc_jpeg_release() frees ctx
with kfree() after v4l2_m2m_ctx_release(). A queued or executing
mxc_jpeg_device_run_timeout() can then recover ctx through
container_of(&ctx->task_timer) and dereference it (ctx->mxc_jpeg,
slot_data, dev_warn) after ctx has been freed.

Cancel the worker from mxc_jpeg_stop_streaming(). The cancel cannot live
in mxc_jpeg_release(): mxc_jpeg_device_run() arms the timer while holding
only hw_lock, not the mxc_jpeg->lock mutex that release holds, so a cancel
in release could still race a concurrent mxc_jpeg_device_run() that
re-arms the timer afterwards. mxc_jpeg_stop_streaming() instead runs inside
v4l2_m2m_ctx_release() -> vb2_queue_release(), i.e. after
v4l2_m2m_cancel_job() has set TRANS_ABORT and waited for any in-flight job
to finish (so __v4l2_m2m_try_queue() will not queue and v4l2_m2m_try_run()
will not run any further job for this context, which prevents
mxc_jpeg_device_run() from re-arming the timer) and before the m2m context
is freed. cancel_delayed_work_sync() removes a pending work item and waits
for a running callback, so the worker can no longer race with the
subsequent kfree(). The cancel is placed before the buffer-release loop so
a concurrently running timeout callback cannot race with it over the same
buffers. If the frame-done IRQ canceled a still-pending timer, this cancel
is a no-op; if the timeout callback has already started, it waits for the
callback to finish. The same mxc_jpeg_stop_streaming() call is also
reached from VIDIOC_STREAMOFF, which drains the worker early, although
STREAMOFF itself does not free ctx -- the use-after-free arises only
when the fd is later closed.

This bug was found by static analysis.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: guest_memfd: Gracefully handle xarray errors when binding a memslot

If inserting a memslot into a guest_memfd's bindings xarray fails,
propagate the error back to the caller, i.e. fail memslot creation as well.
Signalling success and continuing on with memslot creation results in
use-after-free, as the guest_memfd instance will remain reachable via the
memslot after the file is freed (kvm_gmem_release() won't nullify the file
pointer due to lack of a valid binding).

Opportunistically WARN and reject binding if KVM_MEMSLOT_GMEM_ONLY is
already set, partly to guard against goofs elsewhere, but mostly so that
KVM doesn't need to worry about clobbering flags when unwinding on failure.

Regarding the unwind, the slot must be fully prepared before inserting it
into the bindings, at which point the slot becomes reachable.  I.e. waiting
to update the slot in order to avoid the ugly unwind isn't an option.  And
as part of the unwind, explicitly nullify the relevant bindings, as xarray
can store a subset of entries when populating a range.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fsverity: Set S_VERITY only after rollback is no longer possible

Commit f77f281b6118 ("fsverity: use a hashtable to find the
fsverity_info") changed the implementation of FS_IOC_ENABLE_VERITY to
make concurrent reads start going through fsverity verification slightly
earlier than they did before.

Instead of it happening when enable_verity() calls fsverity_set_info(),
it now happens when ->end_enable_verity() sets S_VERITY.

However, ext4 and btrfs can roll back verity after they set S_VERITY,
causing a use-after-free.

Fix that by making ext4 and btrfs set S_VERITY only after rollback is no
longer possible.  On failure, don't roll back S_VERITY, but do roll back
the filesystem-specific verity flag.

Also update enable_verity() to handle any future instances of this bug
more safely by warning and *not* freeing the fsverity_info.

Finally, tweak some comments.  Clarify one, and move information from
another to its proper place in the comment for ->end_enable_verity().

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

accel/amdxdna: clear the mailbox channel pointer when starting it fails

aie2_create_context() allocates a mailbox channel, starts it, and on a
failed start frees it again:

	hwctx->priv->mbox_chann = xdna_mailbox_alloc_channel(ndev->mbox);
	...
	ret = xdna_mailbox_start_channel(hwctx->priv->mbox_chann, ...);
	if (ret)
		goto free_channel;
	...
free_channel:
	xdna_mailbox_free_channel(hwctx->priv->mbox_chann);

hwctx->priv->mbox_chann keeps pointing at the freed channel. That
pointer is the driver's own test for whether a hardware context has a
usable channel: aie2_destroy_context() returns early on NULL,
aie2_sched_job_run() refuses to run a job on NULL, and the message
helpers return -ENODEV on NULL. A stale pointer passes all of them.

It matters on the restart path. aie2_hwctx_restart() calls
aie2_create_context() again on a hardware context that is already live,
after aie2_hwctx_stop() has torn its channel down, and the context
survives a failure there: aie2_sched_job_timedout() discards the return
value entirely, and aie2_hwctx_resume() only propagates it. What is
left is a live hardware context holding a freed channel, and every
later user of it takes the non-NULL branch:

  - the next job submitted reaches xdna_mailbox_send_msg() on the freed
    channel, via the !mbox_chann guard in aie2_sched_job_run(),
  - a second command timeout reaches aie2_hwctx_stop() ->
    aie2_destroy_context(),
  - closing the device reaches aie2_hwctx_fini() ->
    aie2_release_resource() -> xrs_release_resource() ->
    aie2_xrs_unload() -> aie2_destroy_context(),

and aie2_destroy_context() then calls xdna_mailbox_stop_channel()
followed by xdna_mailbox_free_channel() on memory that was already
freed: a use-after-free, and a second free of the same channel.

The AIE4 management channel already does this correctly -
aie4_mailbox_start() clears ndev->aie.mgmt_chann right after freeing
it. Do the same here.

The create path itself is not affected: when aie2_xrs_load() fails,
xrs_allocate_resource() removes the solver node without calling
->unload, and aie2_hwctx_init() frees hwctx->priv, so the stale pointer
never outlives the structure holding it.

Starting a channel can fail today without this patch: the ring buffer
sizes firmware reports are rejected unless both are powers of two, and
request_irq() can fail.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: hackrf: fix use-after-free in hackrf_alloc_urbs() error path

hackrf_alloc_urbs() frees the URBs it allocated so far when one
allocation fails, but leaves the entries in dev->urb_list[] and
dev->urbs_initialized untouched. The caller, hackrf_start_streaming(),
then calls hackrf_free_urbs() on the error path, which walks
dev->urbs_initialized entries and calls usb_free_urb() a second time on
the already-freed URBs, causing a use-after-free (slab-use-after-free
Write in usb_free_urb()).

Drop the redundant cleanup loop inside hackrf_alloc_urbs() and let
hackrf_free_urbs(), which the caller already invokes on error, own the
cleanup of the successfully allocated URBs.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet-fc: fix use-after-free in nvmet_fc_ls_create_connection()

nvmet_fc_ls_create_connection() looks up the association with
nvmet_fc_find_target_assoc(), which returns it with a reference held,
and drops that reference as soon as the target queue has been allocated.
iod->assoc is then dereferenced again by nvmet_fc_makeconnid() while
building the connection id.

The queue only borrows the pointer and takes no reference of its own.
Once the lookup reference is dropped the association is kept alive
solely by the reference taken when it was created, so a disconnect LS or
a remote port unregister running concurrently can free it before

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: prevent session binding in compound requests

A failed multichannel binding can retain its target session on the work
item so that the error response can be signed. Subsequent compound
commands can then use that session together with a tree connection left
over from an earlier command.

Limit binding SESSION_SETUP requests to standalone messages during
message validation, before smb2_sess_setup() can replace work->sess.
Check both NextCommand and the current request offset to cover binding
in the first, middle and last positions of a compound. The existing
validation error path returns STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER and stops
processing the remaining commands.

This intentionally limits support for compounded binding. It is not a
protocol requirement that binding be standalone. Standalone binding and
non-binding compounds retain their existing behavior, without changing
session, tree or response encryption handling.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: cls_flower: avoid stale mask references after delete

Flower releases a mask reference when a filter is removed from the
classifier. The filter object can remain alive while dump, walk, or
hardware reoffload paths hold a reference to it. Those paths can then
dereference f->mask after the mask has already been released.

Keep the mask reference until the filter reference count reaches zero.
Release the mask synchronously from the final __fl_put() while the caller
still holds the tcf_proto reference, and leave the existing RCU work to
free the mask. This keeps the mask available to every reader that still
holds the filter.

The filter is still removed from the classifier indexes immediately.
Therefore, a deleted filter can temporarily retain an otherwise empty
mask; fl_delete() uses the handle IDR, rather than the mask list, to
determine whether the classifier has become empty.

Failed mask assignment can leave fnew->mask as an error or borrowed
pointer without an owned mask reference. Clear it before the common
failure path so the final put cannot release an unowned reference.

This fix does not add fields, snapshots, or per-filter memory.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches with elevated privileges through saved search dispatch and access stored credentials and indexed data or modify lookup data.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly neutralize caller-supplied saved search dispatch values before it places the values into an SPL search.
For more information see Search endpoint descriptions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/leverage-rest-apis/rest-api-reference/10.4/search-endpoints/search-endpoint-descriptions) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, an unauthenticated user could craft a malicious link that, if opened by an authenticated user, executes arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches with the victim's permissions. 
Successful exploitation could allow the unauthenticated user to access or modify data, alter Splunk platform configurations, and disrupt operations available to the affected user.
The vulnerability is possible because the Portable Document Format (PDF) generation component processes request data before it rejects deprecated GET requests and does not apply SPL safeguards for risky commands to subsearches.
For more information see Generate PDFs of your reports and dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/create-dashboards-and-reports/reporting-manual/10.4/report-management/generate-pdfs-of-your-reports-and-dashboards) and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the mc_view_im_data capability could cause the Mission Control incident mapping Representational State Transfer (REST) API to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions. With this access, the user could expose all data in Splunk indexes and all stored credentials and modify protected indexes and lookup data.
The vulnerability is possible because the Mission Control incident mapping REST API does not validate incident identifiers before including them in SPL searches.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Overview of Mission Control in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/mission-control/overview-of-mission-control-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, validate_url_ssrf in src/core/utils.py resolves and checks a hostname but returns the hostname URL rather than the validated address, and session.get in http.get performs an independent DNS lookup when connecting. A low-privileged caller with control of the hostname's DNS can make the first lookup return a public address and the connection-time lookup return an internal address, bypassing the SSRF guard for all modules that call it and exposing readable internal or metadata-service responses. Successful exploitation requires attacker-controlled DNS and a successful timing-dependent answer change between the two lookups. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udf: don't let the extent type hide an exhausted free-space table extent

udf_table_new_block() takes the first block of the free-space table
extent closest to the goal.  It keeps that extent's type and length
together in goal_elen, subtracts one block, and deletes the extent only
if goal_elen then reaches zero.  UDF 2.60 section 2.3.7.1 requires the
free-space extents of an Unallocated Space Entry to be of type 1
(allocated but not recorded), and mkudffs writes them that way.  For
such an extent the type bits keep goal_elen non-zero, so taking its last
block leaves a type-1 extent of length zero behind, starting at the
block after the extent, which is in use.

The next allocation that picks this empty extent returns that in-use
block.  Subtracting a block from 0x40000000 then borrows from the type
bits, and the extent becomes type 0 with a length of 2^30 - blocksize:
about a gigabyte of "free" space overlapping live metadata, the other
table extents and whatever lies behind the partition.  From then on
blocks are handed out twice, or past the end of the partition.

Extents that udf_table_free_blocks() adds are type 0, where the check
works, so only tables written by mkudffs or by another implementation
are affected.  Nothing more than filling such a filesystem is needed:
on a fresh 1 MiB "mkudffs --space=unalloctable" image, creating empty
files until the partition is full writes file entries over the reserve
volume descriptor sequence and the backup anchor, and df then reports a
negative amount of used space.

On syzbot's images the same double allocation is what the two reports
below trip over.  In the first, ftruncate() extends a new file with
enough hole extents to need a chain of allocation extent descriptors;
one AED is placed on another inode's file entry, and a later one is
placed on the block of the AED currently being filled, which
udf_setup_indirect_aext() zeroes, so __udf_add_aext() finds
lengthAllocDescs out of step with its cursor.  In the second, an AED
is placed past the end of the device, sb_getblk() fails, and the error
path of udf_do_extend_file() calls udf_truncate_extents() on an extent
list that no longer covers i_size.

Keep the type separately from the length, as udf_table_prealloc_blocks()
already does.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: Fix duplicate dependency fence releases

drm_sched_job_add_dependency() consumes its fence reference on success
and failure. Do not release the fence again if
drm_sched_job_add_dependency() fails.

(cherry picked from commit e04f3dfb2071451633e6440a3911a9bb65df9144)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu/gfx12: disallow GFXOFF while updating the SPM VMID

gfx_v12_0_update_spm_vmid() does a read-modify-write of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL
over MMIO without keeping GFX powered, unlike gfx11. When GFX is in
GFXOFF at that point the update doesn't stick, and with the SPM VMID
programmed on submission again, the job of a process with a reserved
VMID can still run with the SPM writing through VMID 0.

On navi48, after a few other submissions and a VM fault on the same VM,
a COPY_DATA of RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL from such a job reads 0 although the
update was called for it:

  $ amd_uapi_regression --run-subtest cs-secure-ib-compute,gem-mapping-info-high-va,gpuvm-fault-high-va,reserved-vmid-spm-vmid
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: [gfxhub] page fault (src_id:0 ring:40 vmid:7 pasid:185)
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: 	 Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA1 (0xe)
  RLC_SPM_MC_CNTL in the job: 0x00000000

With GFXOFF disallowed around the update it reads the reserved VMID 15.

(cherry picked from commit 907aebc5578ae09fa5c0e2f0784201295837e60b)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu/userq: validate the moved individual BOs on restore

An individual BO of a user queue VM, i.e. one which doesn't share the
root reservation, goes to the individual needs_update list when it is
evicted. The user queue restore looked at vm->invalidated for them, which
the VM state machine rework turned into the always_valid evicted list and
commit 18decfc9e8cc ("drm/amdgpu/userq: actually validate userq BOs")
into the individual evicted one. That list only holds imported DMA-bufs of
compute VMs though, so for a user queue VM nothing is validated.

The restore then neither locks such a BO nor moves it back. Its PTEs are
updated to wherever it is now, cleared if it went to system memory, and
it doesn't get the new eviction fence, so it can move again under the
running queue.

On navi48, once the BOs of an SDMA user queue are evicted from GTT
(debugfs amdgpu_evict_gtt) the queue faults on its ring and rptr:

  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000000100000000 from client 10
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: 	 Faulty UTCL2 client ID: SDMA0 (0xd)
  amdgpu 0000:03:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000000100101000 from client 10

Validate the BOs on the individual needs_update list like before.

(cherry picked from commit eb0d94765d4be18d41e93ad09947dd9cc06ed31a)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use

When a driver calls dma_free_contiguous() before quiescing DMA, the
page might still have a reference from the device.
put_page_testzero() there returns false, WARN fires, but the code proceeds
to free_contig_frozen_range() putting a live page onto buddy and clearing
the bitmap. A subsequent allocation can hand the same PFN to a new
owner while the original holder still references it.

A concurrent put_page() that drops the last reference between the
testzero loop and free_contig_frozen_range() can double-queue the page
via page->lru, corrupting buddy lists.

Avoid the corruption by not freeing a CMA region if any of the
pages inside are still in use.

Make it explicit in the warning that the driver allowed a leak.

While at it, use page_ref_freeze() to make the semantics clearer and
switch to pr_warn_ratelimited().

[ david: use page_ref_freeze() + pr_warn_ratelimited() ]

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger

__tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which has to be flushed
as an unsigned int. Its callers, tlb_flush_{pte,pmd,pud,p4d}_range(), get
and pass an unsigned long. Consequently, a range that is 4 GiB or larger
gets truncated, possibly to 0.

On arm64 with hugetlb, a 64k kernel can have 16 GiB hugetlb folios
mapped contiguously at the PMD level and flush them when unmapping, and a
16k kernel can flush 64 GiB PUDs through tlb_unshare_pmd_ptdesc(). So
at least these two scenarios are affected.

Fix it by flushing the proper range instead of the truncated one by
properly using "unsigned long" for range_size.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp()

try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() drops the PTE lock after it has cleared the
page table, and takes the PMD lock and the PTE lock to remove it.

In between, MADV_DONTNEED with CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM can reclaim the
page table. The pmd_same() check is supposed to handle this, but it is
only done with CONFIG_SPLIT_PTE_PTLOCKS.

Fix it by performing the check unconditionally.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cipso: fix optlen corruption in cipso_v4_delopt()

cipso_v4_delopt() recomputes the option length by walking the option
buffer after the CIPSO option has been moved out.  The walk then reads
the stale bytes at the tail of the buffer as option data, and a crafted
setsockopt(IP_OPTIONS) buffer can make it treat one of them as an option
length, increasing opt->opt.optlen beyond the valid option data.

The corrupted length stays on the socket and is later used as the copy
length by getsockopt(IP_OPTIONS) and by the udp/raw/ping sendmsg paths,
where it exceeds the size of the buffers they copy into.

Compute the new length from the intact options before the move and
subtract the CIPSO length, and fill the padding with IPOPT_END.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: atl1c: drop oversized RX frames instead of panicking

atl1c sizes its receive buffers from the netdev MTU plus a fixed set of L2
overheads, which comes to 1522 bytes at the default MTU.  A link partner
that sends a longer frame - in practice a MikroTik CCR2004-1G-2XS-PCIe,
whose RouterOS side defaults to l2mtu 1600 while the host stays at MTU 1500
- makes the length reported by the RX return descriptor exceed what the
hardware wrote, and skb_put() then either includes bytes that were never
received or trips skb_over_panic and takes the host down.

Compare the descriptor length against buffer_info->length, the length the
hardware was given, rather than against skb_tailroom(): the skb carries 64
bytes of slack for the DMA erratum, so tailroom is larger than the DMA
buffer and a frame in between would pass the check and still be delivered
with a tail the device never wrote.  The same test rejects frames shorter
than ETH_HLEN + ETH_FCS_LEN; before this change a reported length below
ETH_FCS_LEN underflowed in skb_put().

The frame is dropped with kfree_skb_reason(SKB_DROP_REASON_PKT_TOO_BIG) so
drop_monitor and the kfree_skb tracepoint see it, and counted through
dev_core_stats_rx_dropped_inc(), which survives atl1c_get_stats()
overwriting the hardware counters on every read.  It also counts as work:
atl1c_clean_rfd() has already recycled the RFD, and the refill at the end
of the poll only runs when work_done is non-zero, so sustained oversized
traffic would otherwise drain the ring and stop RX.

Tested on a MikroTik CCR2004-1G-2XS-PCIe (4x AR8151) in a Proxmox VE host,
with atl1c built from a DKMS tree carrying this change: the l2mtu-1600
traffic that panics the stock driver is dropped and counted with the patch
applied, and received normally once the host MTU is raised to match.

This complements commit 36c2009d90f2 ("net: atl1c: fix soft lockup on
out-of-range tpd_cons read"), which fixed the TX side of the same
"host dies while the card resets" problem.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ASoC: SOF: Intel: hda-sdw-bpt: Stop active DMA before closing BPT streams

When sdw_enable_stream() fails in intel_ace2x_bpt_send_async() after
hda_sdw_bpt_send_async() has already started the TX and RX DMA streams,
intel_ace2x_bpt_close_stream() invokes hda_sdw_bpt_close() directly
without calling hda_sdw_bpt_wait().  As a result,
hda_sdw_bpt_dma_deprepare() tears down the DMA buffers and BDL while
the DMA hardware is still running.

Disable any running TX or RX BPT DMA stream at the start of
hda_sdw_bpt_close() before unmapping channels and depreparing DMA
resources.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: Verify the iSCSI ISID is null-terminated

iscsi_parse_pr_out_transport_id() returns the ISID of a FORMAT CODE 01b
TransportID as a pointer into the PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT parameter list,
lowercased in place and never null-terminated.  spc4r37 Table 508 requires
the field to be null-terminated, but a non-conforming initiator can omit
the NULL; when the ISID ends at the end of the received buffer, the pointer
is not a C string.

The registration code still consumes it as one: strcmp() in
__core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg() and in the REGISTER AND MOVE path, and
snprintf("%s") in __core_scsi3_do_alloc_registration(), which also reads
its first 8 bytes unconditionally with get_unaligned_be64() - a NUL check
does not bound that read.

When the parameter list spans more than one page, transport_kmap_data_sg()
maps it with vmap(), and the over-read walks off the end of the mapping
into the vmalloc() guard page and oopses.  Reproduced with a PR OUT
REGISTER + SPEC_I_PT parameter list of exactly 8192 bytes whose final
TransportID carries a 12-byte ISID without a terminating NUL:

  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffc9000138c000
  RIP: 0010:strcmp+0xc/0x30
  Call Trace:
   __core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg+0xd3/0x120 [target_core_mod]
   core_scsi3_decode_spec_i_port+0x8fc/0x13a0 [target_core_mod]
   core_scsi3_emulate_pro_register+0x73c/0x900 [target_core_mod]
   ...
   iscsi_target_rx_thread+0xef/0x1d0 [iscsi_target_mod]

With a single-page parameter list the buffer is a kmap() direct mapping, so
the over-read continues into the physically adjacent page instead of
faulting.  snprintf("%s") then copies whatever follows the ISID in memory
into pr_reg_isid, and PR IN READ FULL STATUS reports the registration back
to any initiator, turning the over-read into an info leak of kernel heap
contents.  Reproduced with a 4096-byte parameter list whose last
TransportID ends at the end of the buffer with a 4-byte ISID and no NUL,
interleaved with I/O to populate adjacent pages: the READ FULL STATUS
response returned the ISID as "0xleak" followed by raw bytes that were not
part of the parameter list.  The snprintf() into
pr_reg_isid[PR_REG_ISID_LEN] caps the echoed ISID at 15 characters, so at
most 11 bytes past the buffer are leaked per command, but the PR OUT
command is not rate limited.

Any initiator that can send PR OUT to an iSCSI-exported LUN can trigger
either variant, including a guest via vhost-scsi.

Require 8 bytes to remain after the ",i,0x" separator, and a NUL inside the
rest of the descriptor, before the ISID pointer is returned.  REGISTER AND
MOVE fails with TCM_INVALID_PARAMETER_LIST; on SPEC_I_PT no target port
claims the malformed TransportID, and the command fails the same way.

The FoE DATA frame handler computes the payload length from the master-supplied mailbox length field and passes it directly to FOE_fwrite. The length is checked against the remaining file capacity but not against the physical mailbox buffer size. A master can declare a large length while sending a short frame, causing FOE_fwrite to read past the end of the mailbox buffer.

Attackers can repeatedly send PUT requests to /api/v2/projects/{id} so recalculateProjectPositions updates every user's root projects, holding SQLite's write lock and degrading availability.

A flaw was found in Quay. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker holding a restricted, short-lived JSON Web Token (JWT) to achieve privilege escalation. Because Quay improperly accepts scoped registry bearer tokens as valid robot account passwords, an attacker can authenticate directly as the robot account and obtain broader permissions. Consequently, unauthorized access persists and enables the attacker to generate fresh tokens even after the robot account's password has been reset.
