Improper following of a certificate’s chain of trust in the remote-attestation verifier used to establish trust with Meta AI's confidential computing backend in WhatsApp for iOS before 2.26.24.72, WhatsApp Business for iOS and WhatsApp for Mac Desktop before v2.26.23.72, WhatsApp for Android before v2.26.23.74, and WhatsApp Business for Android before v2.26.23.70 could have allowed someone positioned within Meta infrastructure to bypass the hardware root of trust by presenting clients with a VCEK certificate signed by a key other than the hardware manufacturer’s. Any such VCEK Cert would first have to be published to the third-party binary transparency ledger used by WhatsApp Private Processing. The ledger shows that every published VCEK certificate chains to the hardware root of trust, confirming no exploitation.

OceanWP WordPress Theme before 4.2.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the oceanwp_edd_terms_list() function in inc/edd/edd-helpers.php, which allows authenticated users with EDD download category creation permissions to inject malicious JavaScript by crafting a category name that breaks out of an unescaped HTML title attribute. Attackers can create a category name containing an event-handler payload that executes in the browser of visitors who interact with the category link on the public EDD archive page, potentially compromising an administrator's session if they view the affected page while authenticated.

The Product Import Export for WooCommerce – CSV Product Importer & Exporter plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author (initial store via wp-comments-post.php) / CSV cell on import' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit requires an administrator to approve the attacker's review, then export and re-import it using the plugin's default column mapping, with the import taking the INSERT branch — which occurs automatically on any site whose database table prefix is not the literal 'wp_', when the CSV has no comment_ID mapping, or when the original review has been trashed. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Simply Schedule Appointments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'payment_method' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.13.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The stored payload is only rendered when an administrator navigates to the hidden support page (/wp-admin/admin.php?ssa-support-admin=1) and triggers the 'Fix appointment durations' action, a condition reliably engineered by the attacker by smuggling a '+1 day' suffix in the start_date field to create a persistent duration mismatch that routes the malicious booking through the vulnerable echo path. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

Admidio before 5.0.18 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to keep account access after a forgot-password reset because User::setPassword() deletes sessions using the visitor ID instead of the reset user's usr_id. Attackers already holding a victim's session or remember-me cookie can continue using it after the victim resets the password, keeping authenticated access to the account.

better-auth 1.3.7 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a race condition in the emailOTP plugin attempt counter, collision-prone email change code keys, and accent-insensitive email lookups. Unauthenticated attackers can send concurrent guesses exceeding allowedAttempts to brute-force OTPs and sign in or reset passwords, signed-in users can verify addresses they do not own, and attackers receiving mail at accent-variant addresses can reset victims' passwords.

rclone 1.67.0 before 1.76.0 contains a credential leak vulnerability in the Ulozto backend that sends X-Auth-Token and X-User-Token headers to unintended hosts on HTTP redirect because downloads use the authenticated f.rest client instead of f.cdn. Attackers who can observe or redirect CDN download traffic can capture the long-lived API key and session token to gain persistent access to the victim's Ulozto storage.

rclone before 1.76.0 leaks credentials in its swift, netstorage and seafile backends, which follow HTTP redirects using Go's default policy: swift and netstorage send auth headers or passwords on cross-host or HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects, and seafile sends API tokens or passwords on same-host HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects. Attackers receiving or observing a redirect issued by the configured endpoint can capture these credentials to access storage or replay signed requests.

A vulnerability was identified in Cockpit-HQ Cockpit up to 2.14.1. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file cron.php of the component Web Worker. Such manipulation of the argument token leads to missing authentication. The attack can be executed remotely. The attack requires a high level of complexity. The exploitation is known to be difficult. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Anacrolix torrent before 1.63.0 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in NewClient within tracker/http/client.go, which unconditionally sets InsecureSkipVerify to true for HTTPS trackers. Attackers able to intercept tracker traffic can impersonate trackers with any certificate, observe info_hash and peer_id values, and return forged peer lists.

Wfuzz through 3.1.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows malicious target servers to inject script by returning crafted links written unescaped into HTML reports. When the links script and html printer are used, attacker-supplied href values close the unquoted anchor tag and execute JavaScript when the operator opens the report.

Reposilite 3.5.27 before 3.6.7 contains a brute-force protection bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to evade login bans by spoofing the X-Forwarded-For header. Attackers can rotate the header value to make unlimited password or token guesses, or forge failed attempts to lock out legitimate clients.

Gunicorn 25.2.0 before 27.0.0 contains an HTTP request smuggling vulnerability in the pure-Python ASGI parser that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to desynchronize request framing by sending malformed framing headers. Attackers can send whitespace-padded Transfer-Encoding or Content-Length headers, signed Content-Length values, or invalid chunk terminators to smuggle requests past front-end proxies to the ASGI application.

Frappe before 15.126.0 and 16.x before 16.55.0 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability that allows Dashboard Manager users to pollute Object.prototype by storing __proto__ keys in Dashboard Chart custom_options. When any user, including administrators, views a dashboard rendering the chart, Object.assign merges attacker properties into Object.prototype, altering Frappe desk client behavior for that session.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in Erlang OTP ssh (ssh_sftpd module) allows an authenticated SFTP user to modify file attributes outside the configured chroot directory.

The SFTP daemon (ssh_sftpd) stores the raw, user-supplied path in file handles instead of the chroot-resolved path. When SSH_FXP_FSETSTAT is issued on such a handle, file attributes (permissions, ownership, timestamps) are modified on the real filesystem path, bypassing the root directory boundary entirely.

Any authenticated SFTP user on a server configured with the root option can modify file attributes of files outside the intended chroot boundary. The prerequisite is that a target file must exist on the real filesystem at the same relative path. Note that this vulnerability only allows modification of file attributes; file contents cannot be read or altered through this attack vector.

If the SSH daemon runs as root, this enables direct privilege escalation: an attacker can set the setuid bit on any binary, change ownership of sensitive files, or make system configuration world-writable.

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ssh/src/ssh_sftpd.erl and program routines ssh_sftpd:do_open/4 and ssh_sftpd:handle_op/4.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 26.2.5.20, OTP 27.3.4.11, and OTP 28.4.3, corresponding to ssh from 3.0.1 before 5.1.4.15, 5.2.11.7, and 5.5.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to ssh before 3.0.1, is affected is unknown.

Observable Response Discrepancy vulnerability in Erlang OTP ssh (ssh_sftpd module) allows an authenticated SFTP user to enumerate the existence of files and directories outside the configured root directory.

The SSH_FXP_REALPATH handler in ssh_sftpd calls relate_file_name/3 with Canonicalize=false, unlike every other SFTP operation handler. This allows .. components in the requested path to bypass the is_within_root/2 check without being resolved. The un-canonicalized path then enters resolve_symlinks/2, which walks up the directory tree above the configured root and issues read_link() syscalls on arbitrary filesystem paths.

An authenticated SFTP client can exploit this by sending a REALPATH request with a crafted traversal path. The server response differs depending on whether the target path exists on the host filesystem (SSH_FXP_NAME when the path resolves successfully, SSH_FX_NO_SUCH_FILE when it does not). This creates a path-existence oracle that an attacker can use to enumerate the filesystem structure outside the configured root, including the existence of sensitive files, directories, and mount points.

The vulnerability leaks only the existence of paths. No file contents, credentials, or write access are obtainable through this issue alone. The information gained may assist further attacks when combined with other vulnerabilities.

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ssh/src/ssh_sftpd.erl and program routine ssh_sftpd:handle_op/4.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.14, OTP 28.5.0.3, and OTP 29.0.3, corresponding to ssh from 3.0.1 before 5.2.11.9, 5.5.2.2, and 6.0.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to ssh before 3.0.1, is affected is unknown.

Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in Erlang OTP ssh (ssh_sftpd module) allows an authenticated SFTP user to render an SFTP channel permanently unresponsive.

The handle_data/4 function in ssh_sftpd contains a catch-all clause that accepts channel data of any type. When channel data with a non-zero type code (SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_EXTENDED_DATA) arrives with an empty pending buffer and a payload at or below the SFTP packet size limit, the clause tail-calls itself with identical arguments, creating an infinite loop.

The SFTP protocol operates exclusively on normal channel data (type 0). Extended data (non-zero type) is meaningless for SFTP and is never sent by conforming clients. However, the SSH protocol permits any channel participant to send extended data on an open channel, so an authenticated SFTP client can trigger the loop by sending SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_EXTENDED_DATA with any data_type_code and any non-empty payload at or below the size limit.

The targeted ssh_sftpd process enters an infinite tail-recursive loop. It never processes another message, its message queue grows without bound, and it can only be stopped by killing the process. BEAM's reduction-based scheduler preemption continues to function, so other processes on the node are not starved, but each stuck channel process consumes its full CPU time share continuously and accumulates unbounded message queue memory. Opening many channels amplifies the CPU and memory impact.

Erlang/OTP SSH configurations using the default max_channels setting (infinity) allow an authenticated user to open unlimited channels per connection, amplifying the attack without requiring multiple TCP connections or authentications.

No file contents, credentials, or write access are obtainable through this issue. The impact is limited to denial of service on targeted SFTP channels, with secondary CPU degradation and memory growth.

This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ssh/src/ssh_sftpd.erl and program routine ssh_sftpd:handle_data/4.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.14, OTP 28.5.0.3, and OTP 29.0.3, corresponding to ssh from 3.0.1 before 5.2.11.9, 5.5.2.2, and 6.0.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to ssh before 3.0.1, is affected is unknown.

Electric Postgres Sync versions below 1.6.10 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows attackers to infer the values of excluded columns by crafting subset where clause conditions against shape responses. Attackers can observe whether subset where conditions match rows to deduce sensitive field data even though those columns are not returned in shape responses, bypassing column-based access restrictions.

Mattermost versions 11.8.x <= 11.8.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.3, 11.6.x <= 11.6.5, 11.2.x <= 11.2.4, 10.11.x <= 10.11.20 fail to bound the time and resource consumption of server-side document content extraction which allows an authenticated user with file-upload permission to degrade file uploads for all users on the server via repeatedly uploading small documents that are cheap to upload but expensive to extract, saturating the shared extraction worker pool. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00694

Spacebar Server before commit 51da17c contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to enumerate complete guild membership by querying the GET /guilds/{guild_id}/roles/{role_id}/member-ids endpoint without guild membership verification. Attackers can exploit the unprotected route handler in the roles member-ids endpoint, which lacks permission checks present in sibling endpoints, to retrieve the full list of member user IDs for any guild on the instance using only a valid bearer token and a known guild ID.

PrestaShop psgdpr versions before 1.4.4 fail to validate that GDPR consent log entries are attributed to the authenticated customer. Authenticated attackers can submit arbitrary customer identifiers to create forged consent records for other customers, corrupting audit logs.

SiYuan versions before 3.8.5 fail to enforce publish access control in the getDynamicIcon endpoint, allowing read-only token holders to access document metadata. Attackers can call the endpoint with type=8 and crafted content to read block titles, names, aliases, and hierarchical paths of restricted documents via template injection.

Contrast before 1.21.0 contains a panic vulnerability in the transit-engine endpoint's ciphertextContainer.UnmarshalJSON function that fails to validate decoded ciphertext length before slicing. An authenticated workload with a valid mesh certificate can trigger a runtime panic by submitting a short base64-encoded ciphertext, causing log spam and request failures without crashing the process.

A hostname canonicalization vulnerability in the email HTML sanitizers of Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) allows an unauthenticated sender to bypass the restriction on forms that target the Zimbra host. DefangFilter and the OWASP ActionAttributePolicy compare the form-action hostname with the request hostname before browser URL canonicalization. A percent-encoded hostname can therefore survive sanitization while the browser submits the form to the normal Zimbra origin with the recipient's authentication cookie. This permits authenticated form requests from a crafted email after the recipient opens it in Classic and submits the form. The issue is present in ZCS 10.1.16 and 10.1.21. It does not bypass an endpoint's CSRF-token checks; a state-changing attack additionally requires an endpoint that accepts the resulting request without that protection.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management product of Oracle Hyperion (component: Reconciliation Manage).   The supported version that is affected is 11.2.26.0.000. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with logon to the infrastructure where Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management executes to compromise Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.4 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N).

Ettercap before 0.8.5.2 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dissector_vnc() in src/dissectors/ec_vnc.c that checks total packet length instead of remaining bytes. A malicious VNC server can send the authentication type and challenge in one short packet to leak up to 3 bytes of adjacent heap memory via the logged challenge.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability in the TIFF decoder that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying a crafted TIFF image. Attackers can provide a malicious TIFF file that, when encoded in a specific output format, triggers a heap buffer over-write causing memory corruption.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain a Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Arbitrary Code Execution.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, and 10.2.9, a low-privileged user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could access file path and metadata listings from search head knowledge bundles via the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This unauthorized access could expose sensitive metadata, including Splunk platform usernames, private knowledge-object configuration file names, installed application directories, and the file path names of security-sensitive configuration and key files.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API actions that list bundle contents and denied files use a capability available to the "user" role instead of requiring distributed-search administration capabilities.
For more information see Knowledge bundle replication overview (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/distributed-search/10.6/knowledge-bundle-replication/knowledge-bundle-replication-overview) in the Splunk documentation. For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with edit permission for containers on only a subset of container labels could modify container pins outside the container labels that the role permits.
The vulnerability is possible because the Container Pin Representational State Transfer (REST) API does not enforce the container label authorization boundary when handling requests.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.4.1/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated Splunk SOAR user with permission to edit and run playbooks could read action status and callback state from a playbook run outside the authorized container-label or tenant scope for that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the playbook API uses mutable runtime context to identify a playbook run instead of preserving the server-provided context.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with permission to view and modify containers with an allowed label could add artifacts to containers that the user cannot view or modify.
The vulnerability is possible because the Representational State Transfer (REST) API artifact-creation workflow does not preserve the authorization boundary for the selected container.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings view permission but not the Assets view permission could view asset names, asset identifiers, app names, tenant names, and ingestion schedule settings for polling assets in the ingestion schedule view.
The vulnerability is possible because the ingestion schedule view does not verify the Assets view permission before it returns data derived from assets.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user who holds a role with permission to view system settings but not assets could view asset, app, and container-label metadata in Ingestion filters.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR returns Ingestion filter metadata without applying asset authorization and tenant restrictions.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.5.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user that holds a role with the System Settings view permission but not the Assets view permission could view asset and tenant metadata in the ingestion history view.
The ingestion history view does not restrict summary results to assets and tenants that the user can view.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with asset edit permission could change the approval requirements and effective automation user for an asset without Splunk SOAR recording field-level audit details for those changes. This could weaken investigation and accountability for changes to security-sensitive asset settings.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not include the asset approval voting fields and effective automation user field in its field-level audit coverage.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with playbook edit permission could cause later playbook conversions to include spurious branch conditions. This can prevent downstream blocks from running in affected converted playbooks.
The vulnerability is possible because the playbook converter retains branch conditions from previous conversions.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to edit and run playbooks could view child playbook status and loop-state metadata for playbook runs outside the authorized scope for that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the playbook status API does not bind the requested run to the current execution context before it returns metadata.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with edit permission on a workbook could configure a service-level agreement at only the workbook phase or task level. Splunk SOAR then flags the task as overdue immediately and does not display the configured deadline in the work queue. The incorrect deadline status could obscure genuine deadline breaches.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR treats an absent phase-level or task-level service-level agreement as immediately due when it compares the configured due times.
For more information see Define tasks using workbooks (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/7.0.0/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/define-tasks-using-workbooks) in the Splunk documentation.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. The Account API endpoint for sharing resources fails to verify whether owner-managed access is enabled and accepts permission scopes not assigned to the resource. An authenticated user can exploit this vulnerability to generate pre-granted permission tickets, causing Keycloak to bypass policy evaluation and issue access tokens with unauthorized scopes.

A flaw was found in Hawtio. An authenticated remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted request URI to monitored endpoints. The FlightRecordingDownloadFacade servlet filter uses an inefficient regular expression pattern that causes catastrophic backtracking when processing certain long requests. This issue leads to excessive CPU utilization, causing handling threads to hang and degrading service availability.

A flaw has been found in hrshadhin CloudSchool up to 3.0.1. Affected by this issue is the function PublicController.checkSanity4Student of the file app/Http/Controllers/Backend/PublicController.php of the component Student Data Access Check. This manipulation of the argument student_id causes authorization bypass. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. The OpenID Connect (OIDC) logout endpoint continues to honor post-logout redirect rules for disabled clients rather than rejecting the requests. If a disabled client retains permissive redirect configurations, a remote attacker can exploit this issue by supplying an arbitrary redirection target in a logout request, leading to an open redirect that can be used in phishing attacks.

A security vulnerability has been detected in XiangLi1999 Diffusion-LM up to 759889d58ef38e2eed41a8c34db8032e072826f4. This issue affects the function main of the file improved-diffusion/scripts/text_sample.py. Such manipulation of the argument out_dir leads to path traversal. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. This product implements a rolling release for ongoing delivery, which means version information for affected or updated releases is unavailable. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

The Contact Form Email plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.72. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to view and delete all stored contact form submissions, create, rename, delete, and clone forms, alter plugin database tables, and persistently rewrite the reporting options to silently email a CSV of all submissions to an attacker-controlled address on every subsequent request. The nonce intended to authorize state-changing POST requests is minted into the same management page the attacker can already render, so it provides no effective authorization barrier against a Subscriber-level user.

The PayPlus Payment Gateway plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 8.3.4 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to generate PayPlus payment page links for arbitrary WooCommerce orders belonging to any customer, overwrite those orders' payment method and PayPlus-related order meta, and trigger PayPlus API calls using the store's credentials — including, when a POS EMV device is configured, initiating a charge request to the store's physical POS terminal. The exploit requires no nonce and no special capability beyond being logged in, as the authorization block is unreachable on the AJAX path due to the inverted isset() predicate.

The Recipe Card Blocks Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.1. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to overwrite the stored post_content of any post or page on the site, including published posts and private drafts authored by administrators or other users.

The UiChemy – Convert Figma, Prompts and AI Builds to Elementor, Gutenberg and Bricks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'head' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.6.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with editor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. On a default single-site WordPress installation, Editors hold the 'unfiltered_html' capability, meaning the plugin's only effective gate passes for Editor-level users, and the secondary UiChemy_Roles check is a no-op on the Free build and default Pro configuration.

The PDF Poster – Let visitors read PDF’s without leaving the page plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.5 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to retrieve the titles and identifiers of other users' private, draft, pending, and scheduled pdfposter posts, and retrieve the title of any arbitrary post by ID across the entire site.

The Recipe Card Blocks Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.2 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to overwrite the post_content of arbitrary posts on the site, including Administrator-owned published posts, bypassing the edit_others_posts and edit_published_posts capability checks. This vulnerability is only exploitable when the wpzoom_rcb_settings_synchronize_recipe_post setting is enabled, and requires the target post to contain at least one Recipe Card block whose twin can be matched to the attacker's draft recipe post.

A vulnerability was detected in itsourcecode Banking Management System 1.0. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file navbar.php. The manipulation of the argument page results in cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used.

Mattermost versions 11.2.x <= 11.2.4 fail to validate that the redirect target on the web app landing page that prompts users to open links in the desktop app stays on the Mattermost origin which allows an unauthenticated attacker to redirect a user to an arbitrary external site via a crafted link. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00893

Missing Authorization vulnerability in ThemeGrill Masteriyo - LMS learning-management-system allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Masteriyo - LMS: from n/a through 3.5.1.
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in Awesomemotive Charitable charitable allows Cross Site Request Forgery.This issue affects Charitable: from n/a through 1.8.15.1.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Liquid Web / StellarWP The Events Calendar the-events-calendar allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects The Events Calendar: from n/a through 6.18.4.

Certain EZVIZ devices are affected by a replay attack vulnerability (CWE-294). An attacker may intercept communication traffic and replay specific control commands, causing the device to execute unauthorized operations.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in PublishPress PublishPress Revisions revisionary allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects PublishPress Revisions: from n/a through 4.3.3.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Andy Moyle Church Admin church-admin allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Church Admin: from n/a through 5.1.11.

The Simple Membership WP user Import plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.2 This is due to missing or incorrect nonce validation on the add function. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to import arbitrary WordPress users into Simple Membership and modify their WordPress role via the plugin's membership-level-to-role mapping via a forged request granted they can trick a site administrator into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Omnisend Newsletters, Email Marketing, SMS and Popups by Omnisend omnisend allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Newsletters, Email Marketing, SMS and Popups by Omnisend: from n/a through 1.9.1.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Magepeople inc. Taxi Booking Manager for WooCommerce ecab-taxi-booking-manager allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Taxi Booking Manager for WooCommerce: from n/a through 2.2.10.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in myCred myCred mycred allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects myCred: from n/a through 4.0.3.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in weDevs Dokan dokan-lite allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Dokan: from n/a through 5.3.4.

Open5GS AMF through 2.8.0 contains a resource leak vulnerability that allows authenticated UEs to exhaust the session pool by triggering failed DNN or S-NSSAI validation. Attackers can repeat PDU Session Establishment Requests with different PDU Session Identity values, leaving stale amf_sess contexts that degrade service for other subscribers.

Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.1, 11.7.x <= 11.7.14, 11.10.x <= 11.10.4 fail to restrict the broadcast scope of group WebSocket events to sessions permitted to read the group which allows an authenticated user, including guests, to obtain the display name, description, member count and member IDs of non-referenceable groups via the received_group event emitted when a group is created, updated, deleted or restored. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00731

The GiveWP – Donation Plugin and Fundraising Platform plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in all versions up to, and including, 4.16.7.2. This is due to missing nonce validation on the `give_render_donor_view()` function. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to reassign an arbitrary GiveWP donor record to an arbitrary WordPress user via a forged request granted they can trick a site administrator into performing an action such as clicking on a link. The resulting association changes donor-account ownership and can satisfy the linked-donor precondition for a separately tracked account-takeover vulnerability (CVE-2026-82675).

LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the HTML bookmark import action in app/Actions/ImportHtmlBookmarks.php uses the global Link::whereUrl() lookup instead of restricting duplicate detection to the importing user. An authenticated user can submit a chosen URL and distinguish the skipped response count from the queued count to learn whether any account has saved that URL, including as a PRIVATE bookmark. The oracle reveals URL existence but does not directly return the bookmark contents or owner. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the authenticated GET /lists/{list}/feed and GET /tags/{tag}/feed handlers in app/Http/Controllers/App/FeedController.php use integer route model binding without an object-level authorization or visibility check. Unlike the web list controller, which invokes LinkListPolicy::view(), the feed controller lets a normal authenticated user enumerate another user's private list or tag and receive its name and feed metadata, along with public or internal bookmark entries associated with that taxonomy. The existing per-link visibility filter still excludes PRIVATE link records, so the disclosure is limited to the private taxonomy and its non-private member links. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.2, sl_createCNIDArray in etc/afpd/spotlight.c assumes every element of kMDQueryItemArray points to an eight-byte uint64_t and copies sizeof(uint64_t) bytes from the indexed p->dd_talloc_array element without validating the element's talloc type or allocation size. An authenticated AFP client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can use FPSpotlightRPC to supply a mixed-type sl_array_t containing a shorter boolean, nil, or string element, and an unauthenticated client can reach the same path when the optional guest UAM and a guest-accessible volume are enabled. The resulting eight-byte read extends beyond the shorter element's heap allocation and supplies an internal CNID filter; no confidentiality channel, write primitive, or code execution was demonstrated, while a production crash would require additional heap placement conditions. The container-type validation added for CVE-2023-42464 does not validate each element inside an accepted sl_array_t and therefore does not resolve this issue. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

A vulnerability was determined in Soar Cloud System Human Resources up to 7.3.2026.0112. This impacts an unknown function of the file /client.aspx. Executing a manipulation can lead to cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A flaw has been found in continuedev continue up to 2.1.0. This affects the function DataLogger.logDevData of the file core/data/log.ts of the component Dev Data Logging. This manipulation causes information disclosure. The attack can be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

devpi-server before 6.21.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write files outside the +files storage root by naming a user and index '..'. Attackers can self-register a '..' user, create a '..' index, and upload release files with attacker-chosen filenames and contents into a parent of the server directory.

The Salon Booking System – Appointment Booking for Salons, Barbershops & Spas plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 10.31.16. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to overwrite arbitrary users' user meta fields, including the _sln_phone and _sln_sms_prefix meta of administrator accounts, and create bookings attributed to arbitrary users. This is exploitable on default installations because reCAPTCHA is disabled by default, causing the booking endpoint's permission check to return true for any authenticated user without a meaningful authorization gate.

The WSMS (formerly WP SMS): SMS Notifications, OTP Login and WooCommerce SMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 7.2.14. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to send arbitrary SMS messages to attacker-chosen phone numbers from the site's trusted sender ID, incurring per-message gateway charges to the site owner and enabling SMS spam or phishing campaigns.

EOE_set_ip reads each network parameter field (MAC, IP, subnet, gateway, DNS IP, DNS name) from the mailbox payload before checking whether the payload is large enough to contain them. The single bounds check at the end of the function does not prevent the reads from happening. A master can send a Set-IP frame with all flags set and mbxheader.length equal to the minimum, causing all reads to access memory past the end of the payload.

The CoE entry gate accepts frames with mbxheader.length as low as COE_MINIMUM_LENGTH (8), but a normal SDO Download requires at least COE_HEADERSIZE (10) bytes of CoE payload to carry its header fields. With mbxheader.length of 8 or 9, the segmented-transfer branch misevaluates due to unsigned wrap, leaving the declared SDO size unclamped. copy2mbx then reads that many bytes starting past the end of the actual payload and writes them into the object buffer.

FOE_read and FOE_write store the filename length as uint8_t, truncating it modulo 256. When (mbxheader.length - ESC_FOEHSIZE) is a multiple of 256, the length becomes 0. Additionally, a request whose mailbox length equals ESC_FOEHSIZE exactly also produces a length of 0 without any truncation. In both cases FOE_fopen calls strncmp with a length of 0, which always returns equal, so the first registered file whose password is 0 is opened regardless of the filename the master sent.

SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in LAN sync that allows adjacent unauthenticated attackers to obtain device metadata by advertising a counterfeit peer with a replayed discovery tag. The client sends the sync scope ID, device name, OS, app version, and TLS client certificate to /peer-sync/v1/session/open before validating the server proof.

Grav API plugin from 1.0.16 before 1.1.11 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows scoped API key holders to override page permission rules because checks read the owning account's authority instead of the key's scopes. Attackers can use keys minted on super-admin accounts to edit, delete or read pages that deny those actions, or use media-scoped keys to change media on read-only pages.

Admidio from 5.0.17 before 5.0.18 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated regular users to upload images into the announcements module by abusing the CKEditor upload handler. Attackers can send id=ann_description to ckeditor_upload_handler.php to store images under adm_my_files/announcements/images and retrieve them via show_image.php, abusing the application as an image host.

Vikunja from 0.21.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to exhaust memory and CPU by creating tasks with many reminders and long titles. Attackers can store a task whose ParseAlarms rendering in pkg/caldav/caldav.go uses quadratic string concatenation, causing every CalDAV read, including other members' automatic syncs, to allocate gigabytes.

Vikunja from 0.20.5 before 2.8.0 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the OpenID Connect callback in OpenIdAuth.vue that accepts a valueless state parameter. Attackers can send a crafted callback link with an empty state and their own authorization code to silently log victims into the attacker's account and view the victims' entered data.

Vikunja from 2.2.0 before 2.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read other users' private projects through the tasks.overdue webhook payload. Attackers can register a personal tasks.overdue webhook with one subscribed overdue task, then receive project titles, descriptions, and owner IDs from other users' reminders at external URLs.

OpenRemote from 1.2.0 before 1.34.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in AlarmFacade that allows restricted users with write:rules to create alarms for assets outside their ruleset subtree. Attackers can deploy a JSON asset-scoped ruleset using target.custom asset ids to create HIGH severity alarms and trigger operator notifications about arbitrary in-realm assets.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass that allows users with the read-only VIEWER role to modify database schema, because CREATE on a nonexistent table implicitly defines it without the DEFINE TABLE permission check applied to explicit definitions. Authenticated VIEWER users can issue CREATE statements in non-STRICT databases to add arbitrary empty SCHEMALESS tables, cluttering schemas or colliding with application table names.

SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in filter_fields_by_permission that allows authenticated record users to read denied child field values. Attackers can query rows where overlapping items[*] and items[*].secret permissions compact arrays, causing shifted elements to retain field values denied by SELECT permissions.

better-auth from 0.8.1-beta.5 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, and @better-auth/passkey from 1.6.25 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, let revoked sessions stay valid because secondary storage session lists are updated non-atomically and some routes trust cookie-cached sessions. An attacker holding a valid session can evade bulk revocation or bans, or use a revoked cached session to register a passkey or create a lasting session.

ArcadeDB 26.2.1 before 26.11.1 contains an observable response discrepancy in MCPToolUtils.resolveDatabase, which checks database existence before authorization and returns distinct 'not authorized' and 'does not exist' errors; separately, a failed Bolt LOGON from READY leaves the previous principal bound after RESET. Authenticated MCP callers can enumerate names of databases they are not granted by probing tools such as query or get_schema.

ArcadeDB 21.10.1 before 26.11.1 contains a resource-limit bypass vulnerability that allows restricted users to evade per-group readTimeout because limits are applied to shared cached statements and plans. Attackers can run SQL text previously cached by an unrestricted principal to skip timeouts, or impose their own timeout and limit on root and other users.

Rclone 1.49.0 before 1.76.0 contains an improper authentication vulnerability in Proxy.Call that lets revoked users keep access because cached auth-proxy answers are never revalidated. Revoked users of serve sftp, ftp, http, or webdav can reconnect within five minutes using their original credentials to retain access indefinitely.

Coder 2.6.0 before 2.29.26, 2.30.0 before 2.34.18, 2.35.0 before 2.37.10, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.6 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability because CSRF exemption patterns in coderd/httpmw/csrf.go are matched as unanchored regular expressions, letting affected API routes skip CSRF token and same-origin checks. Attackers controlling a page same-site with the deployment can make signed-in users' browsers send forged POST requests that recreate dev containers or add users whose names contain derp to organizations.

Frappe ERPNext 8.2.5 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in Manufacturing module endpoints that check only document-type write access, not permission on each Work Order. Authenticated users restricted by User Permissions can send crafted requests naming another company's Work Order to stop, resume or close it.

Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the Buying module: the endpoint that closes and reopens Purchase Orders checks only document-type write permission, not per-document User Permissions. Authenticated users with Purchase Order write access can send crafted requests naming another company's Purchase Order to change its status.

Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in a Selling module endpoint that checks only document-type write permission, not permission on each Sales Order, when closing or reopening Sales Orders. Authenticated users restricted by User Permissions can send crafted requests naming another company's Sales Order to close or reopen it outside their restriction.

Frappe ERPNext 14.47.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Accounts module where a method on accounting vouchers creates and submits Repost Accounting Ledger documents with permission checks skipped. Authenticated users with read access to a Sales Invoice, Purchase Invoice, Payment Entry, Journal Entry, or Purchase Receipt can call it to delete and repost that voucher's General Ledger entries, an action restricted to System Managers.

Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the make_merge_log endpoint that allows authenticated users to read POS Invoice data. Attackers can supply POS Invoice names outside their permitted scope to retrieve each invoice's customer, posting date, and grand total.

Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing validation vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that fails to verify reserved item rows belong to the target Sales Order. Authenticated users with the Stock User role can send crafted reservation requests naming another order's item row to reserve stock beyond that order's limits, creating mismatched Stock Reservation Entries.

Frappe ERPNext 15.87.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that changes Period Closing Voucher job status without permission checks and accepts a request method triggerable cross-site. Authenticated users without an Accounts role, or cross-site pages opened by authenticated users, can send requests naming a scheduled job to stop accounting jobs from completing.

Frappe ERPNext 15.94.2 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in a supplier portal endpoint whose party identity check ignores party type, failing to distinguish a Customer and a Supplier that share a name. Authenticated users, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming records outside their permitted scope to read buying-portal records.

Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains an authorization flaw in the customer portal Issue list, which scopes records differently from the detail view and skips permission checks on requested records. Authenticated users, including portal users without roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read other customers' Issues.

Frappe ERPNext 16.0.1 before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock dashboard chart endpoint that returns site-wide stock value when the caller has no permitted warehouse. Authenticated users with common operational roles can send crafted requests naming records outside their scope to read stock value data beyond their permissions.

Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Projects module endpoint that returns employee costing and billing rates without record-level permission checks. Authenticated users, including portal users or users without roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read other employees' activity cost rates.

Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.121.4 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read POS Profile cashier lists by calling a POS endpoint lacking record permission checks. Attackers, including portal users or users with no roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope POS Profiles to retrieve their cashier data.

A vulnerability was determined in wiroai Wiro-MCP up to 1.3.0. This affects the function upload_file of the file src/tools/upload-file.ts of the component File Upload. This manipulation of the argument url causes server-side request forgery. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. Upgrading to version 1.3.1 is able to mitigate this issue. Patch name: ac61f79888fd36fae8e282995847e542c4ef1cbd. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

OpenAirInterface CN5G SMF through 2.2.2 contains a missing resource release vulnerability in handle_pdu_session_release_sm_context_request() that fails to delete N7 SM policy associations at the PCF. Authenticated UEs can repeatedly establish and release PDU sessions through the AMF-initiated Release SM Context path to accumulate stale associations and exhaust PCF memory.

OpenAirInterface CN5G PCF through 2.2.2 contains a memory leak vulnerability in pcf_smpc::delete_sm_policy_handler() that leaves stale UE IPv4, SUPI and DNN index entries after association deletion. Attackers can trigger repeated SM policy create and delete cycles over N7 via PDU session establishment and release to grow PCF memory without bound and break association lookups.

Donetick before 0.1.86 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to delete other users' files by storing a crafted image value via PUT /api/v1/users. Attackers can set their image to a traversal key and upload a new profile photo, causing storage.Delete to remove other users' attachments or photos under the storage root.

Donetick through 0.1.86 contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows self-registered users to make the server send requests by setting unvalidated circle webhook or Discord notification URLs. Attackers can point these URLs at loopback or internal services, causing EventsProducer and the Discord notifier to POST partly attacker-influenced bodies to internal network hosts.

ByteStash 1.5.0 before 1.6.1 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the /api/auth/oidc/callback handler because OIDC state is not bound to the initiating browser. Attackers can start an OIDC login with their own account and lure victims into opening the withheld callback URL, logging them into the attacker's account to read saved snippets.

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to retain account access because the POST /reset_password/passkey/end handler never calls endUserSessions(). Attackers holding a stolen session cookie keep authenticated access to the victim's account even after the victim recovers it by registering a new passkey.

Linkwarden before 2.17.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the archive upload handler that allows collection members with only add permission to modify other users' links. Attackers can send POST requests to /api/v1/archives/<linkId> to replace another user's stored screenshot, PDF, readable, or HTML archive with attacker-supplied content.

HumHub before 1.19.4 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in GroupController actionNewMemberSearch and actionAdminUserSearch, which skip the checkGroupAccess check. A manager of any single group can query admin-user-search and new-member-search with another group's id parameter to enumerate members, including administrators.

A security vulnerability has been detected in xuxueli xxl-job 3.5.0/3.5.1-SNAPSHOT. The affected element is the function insert/update of the file admin/src/main/java/com/xxl/job/admin/business/controller/JobGroupController.java of the component Group Management. The manipulation of the argument addressList leads to cross-site request forgery. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection') vulnerability in ninenines cowlib allows SSE event splitting and injection via unvalidated field values.

cow_sse:event/1 in cowlib guards the id and event fields against \n but not against bare \r, and the internal prefix_lines/2 function used for data and comment fields splits only on \n. Because the SSE specification requires decoders to treat \r\n, \r, and \n as equivalent line terminators, an attacker who controls any of these fields can inject additional SSE lines and forge a complete event with an arbitrary event type and data payload on the receiving end. In typical deployments where browser EventSource clients or other SSE consumers dispatch on event.type and render event.data, this enables event splitting, client-side logic manipulation, and stored-XSS-equivalent behaviour when event data is inserted into the DOM.

This issue affects cowlib: from 2.5.0 before 2.16.1.

SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 prints SURREAL_PASS and SURREAL_TOKEN environment variable values in clear text in the --help and -h output of CLI commands such as surreal start, sql, import, export, and mcp, because the arguments do not set clap's hide_env_values. Anyone who later sees that terminal output, for example in shell logs, CI logs, or screen shares, can obtain root database credentials.

rclone from 1.59.0 before 1.76.0 contains a confinement escape in the local backend's setXattr function that lets attackers write user.* extended attributes outside the destination root via a planted symlink. Attackers who plant a symlink to an outside directory with a pre-existing child can use --links --metadata operations to set attacker-chosen user.* xattrs on files outside the destination.

ntop nDPI through 6.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read and unsigned length underflow in ndpi_serializer_get_buffer() in src/lib/ndpi_serializer.c when stripping leading NUL and space bytes. Buffers holding only spaces or NULs, or a used length of 0 set through ndpi_serializer_set_buffer_len(), cause reads past the heap buffer or a wrapped 4294967295 length, crashing the embedding application.

FreeRDP before 3.33.1 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the WinPR wLinkedList collection because LinkedList_FreeNode() frees nodes without updating the cached list->current enumerator pointer. When calling code removes the node the enumerator references, LinkedList_Enumerator_MoveNext() or LinkedList_Enumerator_Current() reads freed heap memory, which can crash the process.

Improper Input Validation vulnerability in qs (parse modules) allows HTTP DoS.

This issue affects qs: < 6.14.1.


Summary





The arrayLimit option in qs did not enforce limits for bracket notation (a[]=1&a[]=2), only for indexed notation (a[0]=1). This is a consistency bug; arrayLimit should apply uniformly across all array notations.



Note: The default parameterLimit of 1000 effectively mitigates the DoS scenario originally described. With default options, bracket notation cannot produce arrays larger than parameterLimit regardless of arrayLimit, because each a[]=valueconsumes one parameter slot. The severity has been reduced accordingly.

Details





The arrayLimit option only checked limits for indexed notation (a[0]=1&a[1]=2) but did not enforce it for bracket notation (a[]=1&a[]=2).



Vulnerable code (lib/parse.js:159-162):



if (root === '[]' && options.parseArrays) {
    obj = utils.combine([], leaf);  // No arrayLimit check
}







Working code (lib/parse.js:175):



else if (index <= options.arrayLimit) {  // Limit checked here
    obj = [];
    obj[index] = leaf;
}







The bracket notation handler at line 159 uses utils.combine([], leaf) without validating against options.arrayLimit, while indexed notation at line 175 checks index <= options.arrayLimit before creating arrays.





PoC





const qs = require('qs');
const result = qs.parse('a[]=1&a[]=2&a[]=3&a[]=4&a[]=5&a[]=6', { arrayLimit: 5 });
console.log(result.a.length);  // Output: 6 (should be max 5)







Note on parameterLimit interaction: The original advisory's "DoS demonstration" claimed a length of 10,000, but parameterLimit (default: 1000) caps parsing to 1,000 parameters. With default options, the actual output is 1,000, not 10,000.

Impact



Consistency bug in arrayLimit enforcement. With default parameterLimit, the practical DoS risk is negligible since parameterLimit already caps the total number of parsed parameters (and thus array elements from bracket notation). The risk increases only when parameterLimit is explicitly set to a very high value.

Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers vulnerability in Erlang/OTP kernel (inet_res, inet_db modules) allows DNS Cache Poisoning.

The built-in DNS resolver (inet_res) uses a sequential, process-global 16-bit transaction ID for UDP queries and does not implement source port randomization. Response validation relies almost entirely on this ID, making DNS cache poisoning practical for an attacker who can observe one query or predict the next ID. This conflicts with RFC 5452 recommendations for mitigating forged DNS answers.

inet_res is intended for use in trusted network environments and with trusted recursive resolvers. Earlier documentation did not clearly state this deployment assumption, which could lead users to deploy the resolver in environments where spoofed DNS responses are possible.

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/kernel/src/inet_db.erl and lib/kernel/src/inet_res.erl.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 26.2.5.19, OTP 27.3.4.10, and OTP 28.4.2, corresponding to kernel from 3.0 before 9.2.4.11, 10.2.7.4, and 10.6.2.

Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in Erlang OTP public_key (pubkey_ocsp module) allows forged OCSP responses signed with an expired responder certificate to be accepted as valid.

OCSP response verification in pubkey_ocsp:verify_response/5 and pubkey_ocsp:is_authorized_responder/3 in lib/public_key/src/pubkey_ocsp.erl does not check the validity period (notBefore/notAfter) of the OCSP responder certificate. An attacker who has obtained the private key of an expired CA-designated OCSP responder certificate can forge OCSP responses that Erlang/OTP accepts as valid.

This affects TLS clients using OCSP stapling via the ssl application: a malicious or compromised server can present a revoked TLS certificate together with a forged OCSP response signed by an expired responder key, and the client will accept the revoked certificate as valid. It also affects applications calling public_key:pkix_ocsp_validate/5 directly, where the impact depends on the use case — server-side client certificate validation using this API may allow authentication bypass with a revoked client certificate.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 27.0 before OTP 27.3.4.12, OTP 28.5.0.1, and OTP 29.0.1, corresponding to public_key from 1.16 before 1.17.1.3, 1.20.3.1, and 1.21.1.

Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection') vulnerability in wojtekmach Req allows multipart parameter smuggling via attacker-influenced part metadata.

Req.Utils.encode_form_part/2 in lib/req/utils.ex builds the per-part headers by interpolating the caller-supplied name, filename, and content_type values directly into the content-disposition and content-type lines with no escaping or CRLF stripping. A value containing ", \r, or \n closes the surrounding quoted value and starts a new header line; an additional \r\n--<boundary> terminates the current part and prepends a smuggled part of the attacker's choosing.

This is reachable through every supported way of supplying a part. It is particularly easy when value is a %File.Stream{}, because filename then defaults to Path.basename(stream.path) and POSIX filenames may legitimately contain \r and \n. Any application that forwards user-controlled filenames (or field names / MIME types) through Req.post/2 with form_multipart: lets an attacker inject arbitrary headers into the outgoing multipart body or smuggle additional fields and parts into the request the victim service sends downstream.

This issue affects req: from 0.5.3 before 0.6.0.

Improper Enforcement of Message Integrity During Transmission in a Communication Channel vulnerability in Erlang/OTP ssl (tls_gen_connection module) allows a network-positioned attacker to inject unauthenticated plaintext that the TLS client application later treats as authenticated server data.

The function tls_gen_connection:handle_protocol_record/3 rejects APPLICATION_DATA records that arrive in pre-handshake states when the TLS endpoint acts as a server, but does not apply the same check when the endpoint acts as a client. A network-positioned attacker can send plaintext APPLICATION_DATA records to the client during the handshake. The records are buffered and, once the handshake completes successfully, delivered to the application as if they were authenticated post-handshake data. The attacker cannot observe the client's response or steer the connection, so the impact is limited to blind injection of unauthenticated bytes. The injection window is wider for TLS versions prior to TLS 1.3 than for TLS 1.3.

This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ssl/src/tls_gen_connection.erl.

TLS 1.3 is affected starting with OTP 22.0, when TLS 1.3 support was added.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.14, OTP 28.5.0.3, and OTP 29.0.3, corresponding to ssl from 5.3.4 before 11.2.12.10, 11.6.0.3, and 11.7.3. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to ssl before 5.3.4, is affected is unknown.

Snipe-IT versions >= 7.0.12 and <= 8.6.3 contain an authorization bypass in the Livewire importer component (App\Livewire\Importer, mounted at the imports.index route). The component only checked the broad 'import' ability at mount time, while its files() and activeFile() computed properties queried the imports table with no owner or company scope. As a result, any authenticated non-superuser holding the import permission could view every Import record on the instance (original filename, file_path, filesize, import_type and creation timestamp) and could invoke the selectFile($id) Livewire action with any auto-incrementing Import ID to load another user's record, exposing its stored preview data (header_row column headers and first_row, the first data row of the CSV). Because import CSVs commonly contain personal data, asset serial numbers and license keys, this discloses sensitive information; in Full Multiple Companies Support (FMCS) deployments the disclosure also crosses company/tenant boundaries. Impact is limited to preview data rather than the full CSV file, and superusers were unaffected. Fixed in version 8.7.0, which scopes non-superuser reads to imports owned by the caller.

Contrast (Edgeless Systems) before 1.21.0 performs unanchored suffix matching when selecting per-registry configuration in the imagepuller. Config.registryFor strips a single trailing dot and then uses strings.HasSuffix(hostname, fqdn) without requiring a DNS label boundary, so a registry entry such as [registries."ghcr.io."] is also applied to any host whose name merely ends in that byte sequence, including attacker-registered domains such as evilghcr.io. When an image or layer is pulled from such a sibling domain, the imagepuller sends the configured Authorization header (basic auth, registry token, or identity token), trusts the configured custom CA bundle, follows the configured mirror, and honours insecure-skip-verify (disabling TLS verification) for that host. Image integrity is not affected, as image bytes remain pinned by digest in the policy and are validated after the pull. Configurations that use a leading dot (e.g., [registries.".example.registry"]) are unaffected.

A flaw was found in libarchive. An attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or potential information disclosure due to a use-after-free vulnerability, which occurs when a program reads memory that has already been released. This issue arises when the archive_entry_copy_mac_metadata() function deallocates an internal buffer before completing a data copy. An attacker who can supply input to an application utilizing this function can trigger the flaw to crash the application or read uninitialized memory data.

CakePHP 4.5.12, 4.6.5, 5.1.8 through 5.1.10, 5.2.14 through 5.2.15, 5.3.7, and 5.4.0 through 5.4.3 contain an email header injection vulnerability because SmtpTransport and MailTransport strip only CRLF pairs from header values, an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-77634. Attackers controlling custom headers set via Message::setHeaders() or Message::addHeaders() can insert a bare CR or LF to inject headers like Bcc, redirecting or altering outgoing mail.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a use after free vulnerability in the MSL decoder that can be triggered when processing crafted MSL image files. Attackers can supply a specially crafted MSL image to cause memory corruption, potentially crashing the application or leading to further compromise.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a use after free vulnerability in the EXR decoder that is triggered when a specific memory allocation fails. Attackers can supply crafted EXR images processed under memory pressure to trigger the use after free, causing crashes or memory corruption.

Parse Server before 8.6.119 and 9.x before 9.10.8-alpha.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows LiveQuery clients without the master key to subscribe to installation and internal classes. Attackers can receive installation IDs and device tokens of other devices when these classes are in liveQuery.classNames, then modify those installations to redirect push notifications.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to download data exports by reconstructing predictable file paths under nc/uploads/data-export. Attackers can derive paths from the table id, base, table and view titles, and export time to read full exports, including fields hidden from public shared views.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to identify pending invitees through a distinct sign-in error message. Attackers can submit sign-in requests where validateUser in auth.service.ts skips password comparison for saltless invited accounts, confirming the email address has an account.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 the TFS helper server was exposed on all network interfaces
In JetBrains Rider before 2026.3 code execution was possible via MSBuild configuration files in parent directories

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user could cause Splunk SOAR to store excessive data in the Ingestion Status history through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. When another user with permission to view system settings retrieves the Ingestion Status history, Splunk SOAR could use additional resources and return a larger response, which could degrade the availability of administrative monitoring.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not limit the amount of request data that it records for failed container creation before it stores the data in the Ingestion Status history.
For more information see REST Containers (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/6.4.0/container-endpoints/rest-containers), REST Roles and Permissions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/6.4.0/role-management-endpoints/rest-roles-and-permissions), and View ingested container statistics using Ingestion Status (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.4.1/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-system-health-and-performance/view-ingested-container-statistics-using-ingestion-status) in the Splunk documentation.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When configured with a database that uses case-insensitive collation, Keycloak resolves realm URLs regardless of letter casing. A remote attacker can exploit this behavior by sending requests with alternate letter casing to bypass upstream reverse proxy access controls that rely on case-sensitive path matching. This issue can expose restricted authentication endpoints intended only for internal access, though Keycloak's internal authentication mechanisms remain intact.

A weakness has been identified in sofastack sofa-bolt up to 1.6.12. This impacts the function initSSLContext of the file src/main/java/com/alipay/remoting/connection/AbstractConnectionFactory.java of the component TLS Stack. Executing a manipulation can lead to certificate with host mismatch. The attack may be performed from remote. This attack is characterized by high complexity. The exploitability is said to be difficult. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A flaw was found in certmonger. This vulnerability allows a malicious certificate authority or an attacker positioned on an unencrypted network to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending oversized or deliberately slow responses. Certmonger fails to enforce size limits or transfer timeouts when downloading and buffering Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP) replies over HTTP. Consequently, an attacker can exhaust host memory, drive CPU usage to capacity, or cause certificate requests to hang indefinitely.

request-filtering-agent before 3.2.2 contains a server-side request forgery filter bypass because address validation in src/request-filtering-agent.ts treats IPv4-compatible IPv6 addresses in the ::/96 range as public unicast. Attackers controlling a fetched URL can use addresses like ::7f00:1 or ::a9fe:a9fe to reach loopback or link-local services, including cloud metadata endpoints.

A vulnerability was found in sonos tract up to 0.23.4. The affected element is the function InferenceRulesOp::rules of the file onnx/src/ops/math/gemm.rs of the component Operand Arity Indexing. The manipulation of the argument inputs/outputs results in out-of-bounds read. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 0.23.5 is sufficient to fix this issue. The patch is identified as 44c6f4a7ef988a5bafe98c8bb465d8a253599395. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

Incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs in WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4 could have caused a target's device to reveal its IP information to an attacker if an attacker sent media from an attacker-controlled URL when a crafted Click to WhatsApp ad-reply message was rendered and displayed in a message thread. This issue may have been abused in conjunction with specific spam messages.

@fastify/swagger-ui is the plugin that serves Swagger UI documentation for Fastify applications. In versions 2.1.0 through 6.1.4, the authentication hooks that applications register to protect the documentation are applied to every route the plugin adds except the bundled static asset instance. When the option that serves bundled UI files from a local directory is enabled, that instance exposes every file in the directory without credentials, so a specification file an operator meant to keep behind the documentation login becomes reachable by an unauthenticated client who knows or guesses its name. Access is read-only and limited to files in that directory. The issue is fixed in @fastify/swagger-ui 6.1.5, which applies the same authentication hooks to the static asset route, and users should upgrade to 6.1.5 or later.

Vikunja from 2.2.1 before 2.8.0 contains a TOTP replay protection bypass in ValidateTOTPPasscode that allows attackers to reuse consumed codes by padding them with whitespace. Attackers with valid credentials who observe a used passcode can resubmit it whitespace-padded to the login API within the validity window to obtain a session token.

web-token jwt-framework 1.2.0 before 3.4.10, jwt-experimental before 3.4.10, 4.0.x before 4.0.7, and 4.1.x before 4.1.7 contain a missing integrity check in the experimental Chacha20Poly1305 key-encryption algorithm, which discards the Poly1305 tag in encryptKey() and calls openssl_decrypt() without it in decryptKey(). Attackers on the token path can modify the encrypted content encryption key undetected.

A vulnerability was determined in itsourcecode Insurance Management System 1.0. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file addPayment.php. Executing a manipulation of the argument client_id can lead to cross site scripting. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized.

libexpat through 2.10.0 contains an improper Unicode handling vulnerability in DEFINE_UTF16_TO_UTF16 conversion functions in xmltok.c that can split valid surrogate pairs when output space is limited. In XML_UNICODE builds parsing non-native byte order UTF-16 input, attackers can supply crafted documents that deliver lone high surrogates to character data and default handlers.

Donetick before 0.1.86 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the GET /api/v1/assets/*filepath route that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass URL signature checks by prefixing paths with profiles/. Attackers who know a private upload's storage key can request profiles/../users/<id>/<uuid>.<ext> to retrieve private attachments without a signature or login.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-18 contains a memory leak vulnerability in the ASHLAR coder when an action fails. Attackers can trigger failed actions to exhaust memory resources and cause denial of service.

Uninitialized resource in GPU in Google Chrome prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process to read memory outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

Uninitialized resource in GPU in Google Chrome prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process to read memory outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)
